review_notes: The of of take knowledge of thee joins the participle's unit as the preposition the English light-verb phrase needs to reach its bare object suffix (rule 44), which is how the same idiom is divided at RUT.2.10; the suffix keeps only thee. The competing reading treats the suffix as the rectum of the construct participle and gives it of thee whole under rule 19, but that rule's of + pronoun sentence governs a relation between two nominals, and the subtraction test finds an English verb unable to reach its object rather than a genitive relation gone.
The man's name places the phrase's The on the article of the rectum, an English possessive taking the determiner of the possessor (rule 29).

haYom is divided as an unrepresented article beside yom holding the whole adverbial to day (rules 29, 33), twice. The corpus fuses the pair under rule 30 in eight units; the division was kept because to is the word rule 33 gives an adverbial accusative and no English word stands for the article.
